problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2y\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,0\le x\le z\sqrt{3}},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axes, the line $y=2$ and the line $z=y$ in the first quadrant.
worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2y\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z\sqrt{3}}2y\,dx]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z\sqrt{3}}2y\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}2y[x]_{x=0}^{x=z\sqrt{3}}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}2yz\sqrt{3}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/63a8768b2769fad339ba7667357812d2dda0ea856e846ad666a100f8bc1336e9.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2yz\sqrt{3}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y}2yz\sqrt{3}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y\sqrt{3}[{\int }_{0}^{y}2z\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y\sqrt{3}[{z}^{2}]_{z=0}^{z=y}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y\sqrt{3}({y}^{2}-0)\,dy \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{3}\,dy \\  & =\sqrt{3}{[\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\sqrt{3}(\frac{16}{4}-0) \\  & =4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
